evals.prompt: Show me the latest three public posts from OpenAI on X. I only need one bounded page, not an exhaustive archive; use the direct x-research user-posts command with --summary and include each post's URL, timestamp, and full returned text.
evals.expected_output: A concise, source-backed latest-posts sample from one bounded user-posts request using the deterministic --summary projection, with normalized citation evidence, provenance, returned/requested counts, cursor state, and an explicit completeness limitation.
expectations: Routes an explicit X/Twitter timeline request directly to x-research and invokes user-posts for OpenAI with --summary and a count no greater than 100; does not auto-page, use browser/HTML scraping, jq, or a shell pipeline.
Preserves each returned post's full text, ID or URL, and timestamp for citation; does not claim that summary projection is model-generated analysis or silently require omitted metrics/media.
Reports the requested and returned counts, cursor/has_more when usable, complete, complete_reason, provider, source_url, fetched_at, and unofficial anonymous provenance.
Calls the result a bounded sample or page and never claims it is OpenAI's complete timeline; a missing result is not treated as deletion or suspension evidence.

evals.prompt: Estimate the tone of recent public X discussion about the 2026-08-01 OpenAI release using the fixed query `OpenAI release since:2026-08-01`. Use at most 20 returned posts through one direct x-research search command with --summary, label each positive, negative, neutral, mixed, or unclear from its full returned text, and summarize the sample without claiming to measure all public opinion.
evals.expected_output: A sample-scoped sentiment summary whose classifications are traceable to individual returned post URLs/IDs and full text, whose aggregate counts are reproducible, and whose query, page bounds, completeness, and provenance are explicit. The CLI projection itself is deterministic field selection, not model-generated sentiment.
expectations: Routes discovery directly to x-research search with --summary, the exact whitespace-normalized query, a bounded count at most 20, and one explicit feed; it does not silently fetch additional pages or use jq or shell pipelines.
Classifies only returned full post text into positive, negative, neutral, mixed, or unclear, cites every classified post by URL or ID, and keeps the aggregate counts reproducible.

Labels the conclusion as applying to the returned sample rather than public opinion, explains ambiguity or low confidence, and reports requested/returned counts plus cursor/has_more, complete, and complete_reason.
Keeps provider provenance and timestamps visible, does not present an unofficial anonymous result as an official X statistic, and does not describe --summary as model-generated analysis.

evals.prompt: Investigate whether a widely shared X claim that a major AI company announced a new consumer product today is substantiated. Use one direct, bounded x-research search command with --summary for X discovery, then corroborate the material claim with independent primary or credible web sources. Preserve the full returned post text and citations, separate leads from verified facts, and explain disagreement or uncertainty.
evals.expected_output: An X-plus-web evidence report that identifies the bounded X query and returned posts with full text and citation URLs/IDs, cites independent source URLs and timestamps, distinguishes source roles, records explicit completeness/provenance, and gives a cautious conclusion with unresolved gaps. The --summary output is a deterministic projection, not model-generated news analysis.
expectations: Uses x-research search once with --summary for bounded X discovery/evidence, records query, requested/returned counts, cursor/has_more, complete/complete_reason, post IDs/URLs, full returned text, and provenance; does not call a page-complete news corpus or use jq or a shell pipeline.
Then uses web_search for independent discovery and read for known primary or credible source URLs; does not treat X posts alone as confirmation.
Separates X evidence, first-party announcements, and independent reporting; cites every material claim with its source URL and observed/fetched time when available.

States agreement, conflict, source freshness, and remaining uncertainty; never infers deletion, suspension, or truth from an absent X result, never invents a missing announcement, and never claims the CLI projection is model-generated analysis.
